validity.recommendation: No action — existence, classification, endpoints and capacity are well corroborated. See separate spec concerns for Length and SegmentCost.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, actively-discussed proposed project, not a GEM-only/hallucinated entity. Continuous independent RU/KZ press coverage Jan 2023 -> May 2026: neftegaz.ru (Jan 2023, roadmap signing), kursiv.media (Feb 2023 and May 2024, QazaqGaz deputy chair Arman Kasenov on route/capacity), interfax.ru (Jul 2025, KZ Energy Minister Akenezhov: 'at the idea stage, no documents formally securing the project yet'), and freshest evidence Sputnik/Altapress (28 May 2026, KZ Energy Minister Yerlan Akkenzhanov at the Eurasian Economic Forum: 'we began discussing the so-called Power of Siberia-2 ... up to 35 bcm through Kazakhstan's territory to China'). Multiple named officials (Gazprom's Miller, KZ's Sklyar, Satkaliev, Akenezhov/Akkenzhanov, QazaqGaz's Kasenov) across multiple outlets over 3+ years describe the same concrete route and volumes -- this is not a single unverifiable mention. CLASSIFICATION: transmission / gas is correct -- kursiv.media (2024-05-04, verified OK) describes it explicitly as the trunk pipeline carrying Russian gas in transit to China with a branch serving KZ domestic consumers; this is a major international transmission project, not a gathering/feeder line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 11-pipeline KZ-gas roster -- no overlap. All other rows (Saryarka network P3307/P3308/P3309, Bukhara-Ural P5696, Beineu-Bozoy-Shymkent P5788/P6712, Zhanaozen-Zhetybay-Aktau P5789, Taldykorgan-Usharal P5901, Aktobe-Kostanay P6834, Karachaganak-Uralsk P7819) are domestic Kazakhstan lines; P5410 is the only Russia->Kazakhstan->China trans-border concept in scope. No duplicate. ATTRIBUTION/endpoints: StartLocation=Barnaul (Altai territory, Russia) / EndLocation=Khorgos (Xinjiang, China) matches the route repeatedly described as 'Barnaul - Rubtsovsk - Semey (branches to Pavlodar and Ust-Kamenogorsk) - Alashankou - Khorgos' (kursiv.media 2023-02-24 and 2024-05-04, both verified OK, contain 'Барнаул' and 'Хоргос'): the pipeline is explicitly routed to terminate at Khorgos to tie into the existing Central Asia-China gas pipeline and 'close the loop', with Alashankou as an intermediate waypoint/nearest China exit, not the final terminus. Location [ref] was MISSING_REF -- filled (see fills). CAPACITY: 45.00 bcm/y is well corroborated -- interfax.ru (9 Jul 2025, verified OK) gives exactly '45 mlrd cub. m gaza, iz kotorykh...10 mlrd... na gazifikatsiyu... 35 mlrd... na eksport v KNR' (45 total = 10 domestic + 35 export), and Vedomosti (29 Jan 2025, independent outlet, verified OK) reports Novak revising the figure from 35 to 45 bcm/y in Dec 2024. Two independent sources agree on 45 -- current ref (neftegaz 880528) already passes. STATUS: see status_reviews.

validity.recommendation: Reconcile LengthKnown=1000km against the recorded route to Khorgos -- either the length needs to be extended to cover the full Barnaul->Khorgos corridor, or the record should make explicit that 1000km covers only the domestic Barnaul-Ust Kamenogorsk/Pavlodar leg while the extension to the China border is unmeasured.
validity.researcher_notes: The current Length [ref] (neftegaz.ru, 'Gazprom i pravitelstvo Kazakhstana podpisali dorozhnuyu kartu...', 18 Jan 2023, verified OK) is the ONLY source behind LengthKnown=1000.00km, and it explicitly scopes that figure to a route that terminates INSIDE Kazakhstan: 'Barnaul - Rubtsovsk - Semey - Ust-Kamenogorsk s otvetvleniem v g. Pavlodar s orientirovochnoy protyazhennostyu 1000 km' (~1000km, branch to Pavlodar) -- this sentence never mentions Khorgos, Alashankou, Xinjiang or China; it is describing the domestic gasification leg only, one of two candidate routes under study at the time (the other being Ishim-Petropavlovsk-Kokshetau, ~644km, for northern KZ). But the row's EndLocation/EndState-Province/EndCountryOrArea = Khorgos/Xinjiang/China, and the fuller route as later described by QazaqGaz's Kasenov (kursiv.media, both 2023-02-24 and 2024-05-04, verified OK) explicitly CONTINUES past Ust-Kamenogorsk via Alashankou to Khorgos to tie into the existing China pipeline -- a materially longer corridor (Ust-Kamenogorsk to Khorgos is roughly 700-900km further by any reasonable routing). I could not find any source giving a total length figure for the full Barnaul-Khorgos corridor; every length figure found (1000km, and the alternate 644km route) covers only the domestic segment. So LengthKnown=1000km, paired with an EndLocation on the China border, is internally inconsistent with what its own cited source describes -- the source supports 1000km only for a pipeline that stops at Ust-Kamenogorsk/Pavlodar, not one that reaches Khorgos. This is a genuine spec mismatch, not a rubber-stamp pass. I am not proposing a replacement length (no source states one for the full corridor) -- flagging for Update review.

validity.recommendation: Flag SegmentCost=$4.4bn for Update review -- a real 2023 source supports the exact figure but scopes it to an earlier/narrower (40 bcm) version of the project, and a later independent estimate puts full-project cost 2-3x higher. Do not treat $4.4bn as settled.
validity.researcher_notes: SegmentCost [ref] was MISSING_REF. I found the source of the $4.4bn figure: two Neftegaz.ru articles from ~March 2023 (785077 'Gazprom zavershit razrabotku PTEO...' and 785250 'Glava Gazproma Miller i predstavitel Kazakhstana Sklyar obsudili...', both verified OK) carry near-identical wording -- 'stoimost proekta gazifikatsii sostavit 1,9-2 trln tenge (4,2-4,4 mlrd doll. SShA), proektnaya moshchnost - 40 mlrd m3/god' (project cost 1.9-2 trillion tenge / $4.2-4.4bn, DESIGN CAPACITY 40 bcm/y). This is the top of that range and matches GEM's $4.4bn exactly -- but note it is effectively ONE origin (a single Kazakh-government cost estimate for the 'gasification project', reported near-verbatim by the same outlet twice) and it is denominated at the OLDER 40 bcm scope (30 export + 10 domestic, per Kasenov Feb 2023), not the CURRENT 45 bcm scope (35 export + 10 domestic) that the sheet's own Capacity value reflects. A more recent, genuinely independent source directly contradicts this: Vedomosti (29 Jan 2025, verified OK), reporting on this same pipeline (names the same Barnaul-Rubtsovsk-Semey-Alashankou-Khorgos route) at the current 45 bcm scope, quotes an industry estimate that 'construction of such a pipeline and reaching design capacity would require no less than 5-7 years and cost $10-15 billion' -- more than double the sheet's $4.4bn. I am not resolving this (I cannot tell which vintage the merge should keep), just surfacing that the current value, while traceable to a real 2023 statement, is disputed by later independent reporting at the project's current scope.

fills.researcher_notes: Both kursiv.media articles (same journalist, Zhanbolat Mamyshev, quoting the same Feb-2023 QazaqGaz Kasenov statement in both) explicitly give the route 'Barnaul - Rubtsovsk - Semey (with branches to Pavlodar and Ust-Kamenogorsk) - Alashankou - Khorgos', with Khorgos as the tie-in point to the existing Kazakhstan-China gas pipeline. Ultimately one origin (Kasenov's Feb 2023 statement) republished across a year, hence tier=medium/independent=false rather than high, but it is the best, and only, sourcing available for these endpoints and it is directly on-point.

Kursiv.media published 24 Feb 2023 (verified OK) is the first public detailing of this specific pipeline's route and capacity split (QazaqGaz's Kasenov naming Barnaul-Semey-Alashankou-Khorgos and 40 bcm/y), matching ProposalYear/Month=2023-02 exactly. Note a slightly earlier formal step exists -- the Gazprom-Kazakhstan roadmap was signed 18 Jan 2023 (neftegaz 766922, already cited elsewhere on this row) -- so 2023-01 is an arguable alternate proposal date, but 2023-02 (matching the sheet) is well supported as the date the project concept itself was first publicly described in these terms.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Newest evidence found is 28 May 2026: at the V Eurasian Economic Forum in Astana, KZ Energy Minister Yerlan Akkenzhanov told TASS (reprinted by both Sputnik Kazakhstan and Altapress, verified OK) 'We have begun discussing the so-called Power of Siberia-2 ... up to 35 bcm of gas ... through Kazakhstan's territory to China's territory ... Kazakhstan naturally wishes for the transit to go through our territory' -- i.e. still at the discussion/negotiation stage, no construction, no FID. Both reprints trace to one TASS wire quote (not independent of each other), but a second, separately-reported item -- Sputnik Kazakhstan's own 8 Feb 2026 interview with energy expert Boris Martsinkevich (verified OK) -- adds a distinct, independent data point: he argues the project will likely be realized by repurposing the EXISTING ~80 bcm/y Central Asia gas-pipeline system rather than building new dedicated pipe, targeting a 1 Jan 2030 start, and notes small volumes (~2.8 bcm/y) are already flowing without new construction; no official Gazprom/KZ Energy Ministry confirmation of this approach yet. Together these two distinct origins (official ministerial statement via TASS; independent expert interview via Sputnik) both point the same way: still proposed/under discussion as of May 2026, no change to Status warranted, and genuine open uncertainty about whether the pipeline GEM has recorded (a new Barnaul-Khorgos build) or a lower-volume reuse of existing Central Asia infrastructure is what ultimately gets built -- worth a note for future sweeps but not a basis to change Status, ProposalYear, or the route on this pass. Not stale under the dormancy rule (proposed, evidence well within 2 years).

summary: P5410 is a real, actively-discussed (not GEM-only) proposed Russia-Kazakhstan-China trans-border gas pipeline, correctly classified as gas/transmission with no duplicate in the KZ roster and well-corroborated 45 bcm/y capacity and Barnaul->Khorgos endpoints (Location ref filled); staged two spec concerns for Update review -- LengthKnown=1000km is sourced to a route description that stops at Ust-Kamenogorsk/Pavlodar inside Kazakhstan, not the full corridor to Khorgos, and SegmentCost=$4.4bn (now ref'd) is a real but single-origin 2023 estimate at the project's older 40bcm scope, contradicted by an independent 2025 estimate of $10-15bn at current scope. Status='proposed' reconfirmed against fresh May 2026 evidence (KZ Energy Minister, Eurasian Economic Forum) -- no change. Nothing UNRESOLVED.
